item: Spill folders owner-locked and closed after encryption; benchmarks hold a lease
summary: Open-on-main rows 50-52 and 56. A serve busy at encrypt-in-place is closed with its plaintext offload folder once free (also one swapped in meanwhile, first builds included), and both in-memory builds re-check the encryption under the swap lock. Each spill folder is made as new-<pid>-<id>, flock'd via an .owner file, then renamed in; the sweep trusts that lock over pid and clock (psutil start times move with a wall-clock step on Linux), keeps the pid and start-time rule only for folders without one, and keeps and reports when it cannot tell. The duckdb_tmp root is tightened to 0700. The rollup and source-coverage benchmarks hold a corpus lease for their folder's life and decline inside an exclusive window.
